ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذَا وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ (١) لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ (٢))
What governs «إِذَا» is explained in several ways. The first: it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied "remember" (اذْكُرْ).
The second: it is an adverb (ẓarf) for what is indicated by «لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ», i.e. "when it occurs, it will not be belied".
The third: it is an adverb for خَافِضَةٍ or رَافِعَةٍ, i.e. "when it occurs, it will abase and exalt".
The fourth: it is an adverb for رُجَّتْ; on this view the second إِذَا is a repetition of the first, or a badal (substitute) from it.
The fifth: it is an adverb for what is indicated by فَأَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ, i.e. "when it occurs, the states of people in it will become clear". And كَاذِبَةٌ [is in the sense of الْكَذِب (lying), like الْعَاقِبَة and الْعَافِيَة. It is also said: the implied meaning is "it has no lying state (حَالَةٌ كَاذِبَةٌ)"], i.e. one about which a lie is told. And (خَافِضَةٌ رَافِعَةٌ) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is abasing (خَافِضَةٌ) some people and exalting (رَافِعَةٌ) others". It has also been read in the accusative, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «كَاذِبَةٌ» or in «وَقَعَتْ».

ukberi-tibyan:10-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ (١٠) أُولَئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ (١١) فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ (١٢) ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٣) وَقَلِيلٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ (١٤) عَلَى سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ (١٥) مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَيْهَا مُتَقَابِلِينَ (١٦))
His saying (وَالسَّابِقُونَ): the first is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the second is its khabar (predicate), i.e. "those who were foremost in good are the foremost to Paradise".
It is also said: the second is a naʿt (adjective) of the first, or a repetition for tawkīd (emphasis), and the khabar is «أُولَئِكَ».
His saying (فِي جَنَّاتِ): i.e. "they are in gardens"; or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «الْمُقَرَّبُونَ», or an adverbial (ẓarf).
It is also said: it is the khabar of «ثُلَّةٌ». On the earlier views the sentence is complete at His saying «النَّعِيمِ», and «ثُلَّةٌ» has two possibilities. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is «عَلَى سُرُرٍ». The second: it is a khabar, i.e. "they are ثُلَّةٌ (a multitude)".
And (مُتَّكِئِينَ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «عَلَى», and «مُتَقَابِلِينَ» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُتَّكِئِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ بِأَكْوَابٍ وَأَبَارِيقَ وَكَأْسٍ مِنْ مَعِينٍ (١٨))
And (يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ) may be resumptive, and may be a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (بِأَكْوَابٍ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَطُوفُ.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَحُورٌ عِينٌ (٢٢))
His saying (وَحُورٌ عِينٌ) is read in the nominative, and there are several views on it.
The first: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «وِلْدَانٌ», i.e. they go round among them for enjoyment, not for service.
The second: its implied form is "they have حُورٌ", or "with them", or "and there are". The third: its implied form is "and their women are حُورٌ".
It is also read in the accusative, on the implied form "they are given" or "they are recompensed".
And in the genitive, conjoined to أَكْوَابٍ in wording but not in meaning, because the houris are not passed around.
It is also said: it is conjoined to «جَنَّاتٍ», i.e. "in gardens and in [the company of] houris".
And الْحُورُ is the plural of حَوْرَاءَ, and الْعِينُ the plural of عَيْنَاءَ; its first letter was not given ḍamma, so that the yāʾ would not change into a wāw.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (٢٤))
And (جَزَاءً) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or it is on the implied form "they are recompensed with a recompense (يُجْزَوْنَ جَزَاءً)".

ukberi-tibyan:25-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا وَلَا تَأْثِيمًا (٢٥) إِلَّا قِيلًا سَلَامًا سَلَامًا (٢٦))
His saying (إِلَّا قِيلًا): it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
And (سَلَامًا) is a badal (substitute) or an adjective (ṣifa). It is also said: it is the object of «قِيلًا». It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:32-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ (٣٢) لَا مَقْطُوعَةٍ وَلَا مَمْنُوعَةٍ (٣٣))
His saying (لَا مَقْطُوعَةٍ): it is said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of فَاكِهَةٍ. It is also said: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.

ukberi-tibyan:35-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَنْشَأْنَاهُنَّ إِنْشَاءً (٣٥) فَجَعَلْنَاهُنَّ أَبْكَارًا (٣٦) عُرُبًا أَتْرَابًا (٣٧))
His saying (أَنْشَأْنَاهُنَّ): the pronoun refers to الْفُرُش (the couches), because what is meant by them is the women. And الْعُرُبُ is the plural of عَرُوبٍ (a woman loving to her husband), and الْأَتْرَابُ is the plural of تِرْبٍ (one of equal age).

ukberi-tibyan:38-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِأَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ (٣٨) ثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ (٣٩) وَثُلَّةٌ مِنَ الْآخِرِينَ (٤٠) وَأَصْحَابُ الشِّمَالِ مَا أَصْحَابُ الشِّمَالِ (٤١) فِي سَمُومٍ وَحَمِيمٍ (٤٢) وَظِلٍّ مِنْ يَحْمُومٍ (٤٣))
His saying (لِأَصْحَابِ الْيَمِينِ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَنْشَأْنَاهُنَّ or to جَعَلْنَاهُنَّ, since it is a naʿt (adjective) of أَتْرَابٍ. And (ثُلَّةٌ), i.e. "and they are ثُلَّةٌ". Likewise «فِي سَمُومٍ», i.e. "they are in سَمُومٍ (scorching wind)".
The yāʾ in «يَحْمُومٍ» is redundant (zāʾida), and its pattern is يَفْعُولُ, from الْحِمَم (charcoal) or الْحَمِيم (boiling water).
«[Translator's note: the source calls the phrase a naʿt of أَتْرَابٍ while attaching the lām to the verbs; this is translated as written.]»

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذَا رُجَّتِ الْأَرْضُ رَجًّا (٤))
His saying (إِذَا رُجَّتِ): «إِذَا» is a badal (substitute) from the first إِذَا.
It is also said: it is an adverb (ẓarf) for رَافِعَةٌ. It is also said: for what is indicated by «فَأَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ». It is also said: it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied "remember" (اذْكُرْ).

ukberi-tibyan:52-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَآكِلُونَ مِنْ شَجَرٍ مِنْ زَقُّومٍ (٥٢) فَمَالِئُونَ مِنْهَا الْبُطُونَ (٥٣) فَشَارِبُونَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْحَمِيمِ (٥٤) فَشَارِبُونَ شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ (٥٥))
His saying (مِنْ شَجَرٍ): i.e. "you will eat something from the trees". It is also said: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). And (مِنْ زَقُّومٍ) is a naʿt (adjective) of شَجَرٍ, or of the omitted "something".
It is also said: the second «مِنْ» is redundant, i.e. "you will eat زَقُّومًا from trees". The hāʾ in «مِنْهَا» refers to the trees, and the hāʾ in «عَلَيْهِ» refers to what is eaten.
And (شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ) is read with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra [on the shīn]; the fatḥa form is the maṣdar (verbal noun), and the other two are a noun for it. It is also said: they are dialectal variants of the maṣdar, and the implied form is "a drinking like the drinking of الْهِيمِ". And (الْهِيمِ) is the plural of أَهْيَمَ and هَيْمَاءَ (thirst-crazed camels).

ukberi-tibyan:76-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ (٧٦) إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ (٧٧) فِي كِتَابٍ مَكْنُونٍ (٧٨))
His saying (لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ): it is parenthetical, between the described noun and the adjective. And (فِي كِتَابٍ) is another adjective (ṣifa) of قُرْآنٍ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in كَرِيمٍ, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:79-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ (٧٩) تَنْزِيلٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٨٠))
His saying (لَا يَمَسُّهُ): it is a negation. It is also said: it is a prohibition, [the doubled consonant] being given a ḍamma.
And (تَنْزِيلٌ), i.e. "it is a revelation"; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of قُرْآنٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ مَا أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ (٨))
His saying (فَأَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject). And (مَا أَصْحَابُ) is a mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), [together] the khabar of the first.
If it is asked: where is the referent (al-ʿāʾid) from the clause back to the mubtadaʾ?
It is answered: since the second «أَصْحَابُ» is the first itself, no pronoun was needed.
It is also said: «مَا أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ» has no grammatical position, and likewise مَا أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ and وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ; and the khabar of the first is أُولَئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ. This is far-fetched, because أَصْحَاب الْمَشْأَمَةِ are not among الْمُقَرَّبِينَ.

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تُكَذِّبُونَ (٨٢))
(وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ), i.e. "the thanks for your provision".

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَرْجِعُونَهَا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (٨٧))
And (تَرْجِعُونَهَا) is the answer of «لَوْلَا», and that suffices in place of the answer of the second one. It is also said the reverse. It is also said: the second لَوْلَا is a repetition.

ukberi-tibyan:88-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ (٨٨) فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ وَجَنَّةُ نَعِيمٍ (٨٩))
His saying (فَأَمَّا إِنْ كَانَ): the answer of أَمَّا is «فَرَوْحٌ». As for «إِنْ», the answer of «أَمَّا» suffices in place of its answer, because the answer of «إِنْ» has been omitted in several places; the implied form is "then he has رَوْحٌ".
It is read with fatḥa on the rāʾ and with ḍamma; the fatḥa form is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the ḍamma form is a noun for it. It is also said: it is that by which one is refreshed.
The origin of «رَيْحَانٌ» is رَيْوُحَانُ on the pattern فَيْعُلَانُ; the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and assimilated, then lightened, like سَيِّدٍ and سَيْدٍ. It is also said: it is فَعْلَانُ, the wāw having been changed into a yāʾ even though it was vowelless and the letter before it had fatḥa.

ukberi-tibyan:93-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَنُزُلٌ مِنْ حَمِيمٍ (٩٣) وَتَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ (٩٤) إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ (٩٥) فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ (٩٦))
His saying (فَنُزُلٌ): i.e. "then he has a hospitality (نُزُلٌ)". (وَتَصْلِيَةُ) in the nominative is conjoined to نُزُلٌ, and in the genitive conjoined to حَمِيمٍ.
And (حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ), i.e. "the truth of the certain report". It is also said: the meaning is "the reality of certainty".
And (الْعَظِيمِ) is an adjective (ṣifa) of رَبِّكَ; it is also said: of الِاسْم.
And Allah knows best.
